asignatura: INICIACIÓN A HABILIDADES COMUNICATIVAS EN INGLÉS(B)
resumen:
More than 1.5 billion people speak English; it matters for career, education and personal development (coursepack p. 2).
Globalisation (fast travel, fast markets, 'uniform' culture) has made a global language real (slide 3).
A strong command of English means proficiency in four skills: speaking, listening, reading and writing (p. 2-4).
Each skill is defined: speaking articulates ideas verbally, reading interprets text, writing expresses thoughts clearly, listening receives and interprets messages (p. 3-4).
Practical steps: speak clearly and slowly, focus on pronunciation, read aloud, learn useful sentences, practise with a friend (p. 4-5; slide 7).
Bonus chart: generations X, Y, Z, Alpha and future Beta… (McCrindle and Fell, 2021) (slide 8).

tarjetas.pregunta: What are the four primary skills?

tarjetas.respuesta: Articulating ideas and information verbally in a clear, concise manner (p. 3).
Reading online articles on topics you are interested in (p. 3).
Journaling about your experiences, thoughts or reflections (p. 3).
Thoughts are properly translated into words, avoiding mispronunciations and enhancing understanding (p. 4).
You engage with the text in sight and sound, correct yourself and build fluency (p. 5).
